instructions.workflow: Substantial repository work needs a tracked goal. Read-only investigation is exempt. Follow the node's prompt and this card; ask the human only what the card says is theirs to decide.
instructions.rigor: Assess engineering risk and commitment, and scale requirements discovery from light to thorough with it. Raise rigor when evidence warrants it.
instructions.communication: Follow the repository's documentation and style conventions. Lead with outcomes; add implementation detail only where it helps a decision.
instructions.review: You are one of several independent reviewers, each with one lens; judge only what yours asks, and do not read the other reviews of this subject (`.zzzops/reviews/<goal>/` files of other nodes) before you submit. Approving with no findings is a good outcome. Raise a finding only when you can name what goes wrong if it is ignored: give `impact` (that consequence, concretely) and `material` (true: it must be fixed before the work proceeds; false: a note, preference or idea). An independent filter may promote a note; it never demotes a material finding. On code, target `test_design` for a problem in the tests; `implement` cannot change them. On a re-review, read what changed first (`previous.changed` or `previous.interdiff`) and give every prior finding a status. Check claims against the integration tip (`read_dev`). Write the full review to the artifact and a one-line verdict in `summary`.
instructions.verification: Give observable evidence in small chunks. Product behaviour and reusable test infrastructure need direct tests; documentation does not. Use the smallest falsifiable local check first, then widen.
instructions.code_quality: Preserve behaviour unless the goal authorizes a change. Remove dead code only with evidence; treat generated and vendored code conservatively.
instructions.dependencies: Use project-native tooling, never hand-edit generated artifacts, and change dependencies only within the goal's scope and with verification.
instructions.security: Never expose secrets or mutate production without authority. Repository rules may tighten, never weaken, safety, privacy or compliance boundaries.
instructions.git: Commit normally on the goal's work branch; never rewrite pushed commits; never bypass required checks or merge authority.
instructions.routing: Choose a model at or above the node's capability tier, preferring the listed models. Keep human interaction on the root agent.
